channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Major Blockchains Have Not Been Hacked: Securitize CEO
item.description: Carlos Domingo, chairman, co-founder, and CEO of Securitize, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the biggest ever heist. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Coinbase Gets National Bank Charter Approval
item.description: Bloomberg's Olga Kharif joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Coinbase, the largest US crypto exchange, said a key regulator has fully signed off on its request to become a nationally chartered trust bank, the latest example of firms in the digital-asset space entering the world of traditional finance. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Everybody Will Be Hacked At Some Point: Ledger CEO
item.description: Pascal Gautier, chairman and CEO of Ledger, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The hackers who stole $6.3 billion from Binance last week found a way to take 40% of the stolen cryptocurrency in one hit, reducing their chances of being caught in the act, and it cost them just $15. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Need Crypto Security At More Layers: Anchorage CEO
item.description: Nathan McCaully, co-founder and CEO Anchorage Digital, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the historic Binance hack and the need for increased security measures at every level of digital assets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Board Members Tap Wachtell Lipton to Probe CEO Affair
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s independent board members tapped the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to help probe Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
item.dc:creator: Nick Turner

item.title: How Hackers Pulled Off the Greatest Heist Ever
item.description: Bloomberg's Vildana Hajric joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the biggest ever heist. Around $3.13 billion is with the hackers in wallets linked to the theft, mostly denominated in Bitcoin and Ether. A further $2.85 billion of the stolen crypto was either frozen or intercepted. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NYSE Taps Avalanche For Tokenized Stocks
item.description: Morgan Krupetsky, vice president of Onchain Finance at Ava Labs joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The New York Stock Exchange announced it will settle tokenized stocks for its round-the-clock platform exclusively through the Avalanche blockchain. Ava Labs developed the Avalanche blockchain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google’s Gemini Targets Health Care’s Data Problem
item.description: Google Cloud is launching Gemini for Health Care, an AI platform designed to connect fragmented information across hospitals, insurers and other health systems while reducing administrative work. Aashima Gupta, Global Leader of Healthcare at Google Cloud, discusses how Gemini can connect medical records, clinical guidelines and business systems, and how Google is building privacy, security and HIPAA compliance into the platform. She joins Riley Griffin on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Washington Weighs Nvidia Fallout as China Concerns Grow
item.description: The controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is raising broader national security questions in Washington, from the potential exposure of sensitive information to concerns over the company’s dealings in China. Foundation for American Innovation senior fellow Ryan Fedasiuk discusses the questions he believes an independent investigation should examine and why the episode could add momentum to bipartisan efforts to tighten controls on the flow of advanced US chips to China. He joins Riley Griffin on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Startup Sierra Is an Anchor Tenant for $300 Million Bond Deal
item.description: Rockrose Development Corp., a property developer and landlord, is looking to sell a commercial mortgage bond backed by a loan for two New York office buildings, whose tenants include an AI startup.
item.dc:creator: Scott Carpenter

item.title: Anthropic Targets $1.4T Valuation in Blockbuster IPO
item.description: Anthropic is seeking a $1.4 trillion fully diluted valuation as it prepares to become the first frontier AI lab to go public, testing investor appetite after a sharp selloff in AI stocks. Bloomberg’s Bailey Lipschultz and Rachel Metz break down demand for the offering, the enormous growth Wall Street is modeling to justify the valuation, and Anthropic’s latest Mythos and Fable models. They join Riley Griffin on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s $1.4 Trillion IPO Bet Tests AI Appetite
item.description: Bloomberg’s Riley Griffin breaks down Anthropic's big goal of seeking a $1.4 trillion valuation in an IPO that could raise more money than SpaceX's blockbuster debut. Plus, Nvidia shares are down for a second straight day following the scandal surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy; and SoftBank reports a $7 billion net loss in the second quarter, its first loss in nearly two years. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Scandal Underscores Growing Espionage Risks for AI Firms
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy has underscored how Beijing and other nations are increasingly turning to corporate espionage to gain an edge in the global artificial intelligence race.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Drozdiak

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Finally Comes Out Nov. 19
item.description: The wait is almost over. Grand Theft Auto VI is set to come out on November 19. It's expected to be one of the most lucrative entertainment releases ever. Pre-orders are already at "unprecedented levels." Grand Theft Auto V came out in 2013. Bloomberg Intelligence Technology Research Analyst Nathan Naidu joins Bloomberg Radio with more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hot Inflation Revives December Rate Hike
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Inflation comes in hot, strengthening the case for a December rate hike. Anthropic tests investor appetite with a potential $1.4 trillion valuation, while Nvidia faces fresh scrutiny around Jensen Huang. White House CEA Chair Chris Phelan and Carlyle’s Jason Thomas break down the Fed outlook and AI risk. And Bucks President Josh Glessing on building a franchise beyond Giannis. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation in Blockbuster IPO
item.description: Anthropic PBC is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its initial public offering, in a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence lab to go public. Bloomberg's Bailey Lipschultz joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Unveils Office Tools Ahead of IPO, Taking on Microsoft
item.description: Anthropic PBC is releasing a suite of tools that weave the company’s artificial intelligence capabilities into more everyday office work, a move that puts it in sharper competition with two of its backers: Microsoft Corp. and Alphabet Inc.’s Google.The features, set to be unveiled at a company event on Tuesday, include a video call assistant, a data dashboard tool and a spreadsheet service called Claude Sheets that closely resembles Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets, but with Anthropic’s AI buil
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Diamondback, KKR to Get Stake in Water Firm for $2.1 Billion
item.description: Diamondback Energy Inc. and KKR & Co. agreed to jointly acquire a 70% stake in the oil field water-handling company Deep Blue Midland Basin LLC, a deal that underlines the importance of water in the US shale industry.
item.dc:creator: David Wethe

item.title: CoreWeave Has a Sentiment Problem Even Strong Earnings Can’t Fix
item.description: After a bruising week for artificial intelligence stocks, CoreWeave Inc. faces a high bar to convince Wall Street that the AI trade is alive and well when it reports earnings after the bell.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica
